identity.title: MMQA: Evaluating LLMs with Multi-Table Multi-Hop Complex Questions

problem.claim: Assess LLM understanding and reasoning on complex questions requiring evidence from multiple connected tables and multiple inference steps.

gap.claim: Existing tabular benchmarks such as WikiTableQuestions and WikiSQL focus on single-table scenarios, limiting their reflection of real-world complexity.

contributions.claim: The MMQA dataset evaluates multi-table, multi-hop question answering, including relationships involving primary and foreign keys.
A framework assesses multi-table retrieval, Text-to-SQL generation, multi-table QA, primary-key selection, and foreign-key selection.
A multi-table retrieval method is proposed for the MMQA setting.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors characterize their multi-table retrieval method as novel and report state-of-the-art performance on MMQA against several strong baselines.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that their retrieval method achieves state-of-the-art performance on MMQA compared with several strong baselines; numerical results and experimental conditions are not given in the abstract.
The authors report that both open-source and commercial LLMs perform substantially below human performance on multi-table understanding and reasoning tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: Single-table benchmarks are presented as insufficient for capturing real-world tabular complexity.
MMQA is introduced to assess multi-table, multi-hop understanding and reasoning.
A framework is defined across retrieval, SQL generation, QA, and key-selection capabilities.
A retrieval method is proposed and reported as SOTA; broader experiments report substantial room for LLM improvement relative to humans.

source_observation.claim: The abstract aligns benchmark design, capability dimensions, and reported model comparisons around the same multi-table reasoning challenge.

lessons.interpretation: A tightly matched task decomposition can make an evaluation claim easier to trace from problem definition to evidence.
lessons.application: When introducing a benchmark, map each stated capability to an explicit evaluation dimension and report comparisons within that same task scope.
lessons.exception: This structure may be unsuitable when the target task cannot be meaningfully decomposed into separable capabilities.

unknowns: The abstract gives no dataset size, construction details, model list, human-evaluation protocol, numerical scores, or statistical uncertainty.
The basis and scope of the claimed SOTA result, including baseline configurations and evaluation conditions, are unspecified.
The abstract does not establish that the benchmark improves real-world capabilities; S7 states this as an expectation.
